extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers applying for HFSP Long-Term (LTF) or Cross-Disciplinary (CDF) Postdoctoral Fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for applying to HFSP Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary Postdoctoral Fellowships, including eligibility, scope of research, publication requirements, and review/scoring procedures. Targets applicants preparing a Letter of Intent and (if invited) a Full Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontier / potentially transformative research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports proposals for frontier, potentially transformative research in the life sciences; applications for high-risk projects are particularly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should challenge existing paradigms by using novel approaches and techniques and should address an important problem or a barrier to progress in the field. Applicants are encouraged to consult past HFSP Fellows for examples of funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be interdisciplinary in nature and foster novel collaborations that bring biologists together to focus on frontier problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to applicants who add new ideas or unique approaches to their research, involving learning new methods, changing study system, or exposure to new theory or literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness from applicant's prior work / change in research direction
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research topic must be distinctly different from the applicant’s PhD or previous postdoctoral work and should expose fellows to new theories and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP aims to broaden research skills by moving into new areas; the project should be primarily the idea of the applicant (though consultation with the host supervisor is allowed). Projects that are an obvious next step or a close continuation of the applicant’s PhD or host laboratory research are not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct fellowship type (LTF vs CDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a PhD in a biological discipline or with prior experience in life sciences should apply for Long-Term Fellowships (LTF); applicants holding a doctoral degree from a non-biological discipline with little or no life-sciences experience should apply for Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships (CDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the program that best suits your research background and proposed project. Only one fellowship application per year is permitted (either LTF or CDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and host-country restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may be from any country, but candidates cannot apply for a fellowship to work in the country of their nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nationals of HFSPO Member Countries can apply to work in any country that they are NOT a national of. Candidates who are not nationals of an HFSPO Member Country can ONLY apply to work in an HFSPO Member Country. Dual nationals may apply to work in one of their countries of nationality ONLY if they have never lived in that country and meet one of the first two criteria. In case of doubt, contact the Fellowship Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host country and host institution eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the following must be fulfilled: propose a change in country; propose a research institution in a host country that they are not a national of (see dual-nationality rules); not propose to take up the fellowship in the country where they obtained their PhD; not have studied or worked in the proposed host country for more than 12 months (consecutively or not) by the activation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined duration of all stays (research, internships, degrees, etc.) is counted. Applicants already working at the proposed host institution are eligible ONLY if they arrived on or after 1 April 2026 and must activate the fellowship within 12 months after arrival. For‑profit research environments are not eligible host institutions (collaborations allowed). For international/extraterritorial institutions, the country where the laboratory is located is considered the host country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host supervisor restrictions and endorsement limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate a primary host supervisor (secondary allowed if necessary). Applicants cannot propose host supervisors who are former scientific collaborators, former research supervisors, or with whom they have worked or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are ineligible if the applicant has spent more than 12 months (consecutively or not) working with the proposed host supervisor by the activation date. Any host supervisor can endorse only ONE fellowship application (LOI) per competition year. Supervisors may still mentor previous HFSP fellows or be part of HFSP Research Grant teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD conferral timing and time-since-PhD limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must have completed their PhD (or comparable doctoral degree) before starting the fellowship and before 31 December 2027 at the latest. The most recent relevant doctoral degree date is used to determine eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are not eligible if the doctoral degree was conferred more than 3 years (36 months) prior to the Full Proposal submission deadline (24 September 2026). Therefore degrees conferred before 24 September 2023 are ineligible, except for specified exemptions. Applicants may request exemptions for specific post-PhD career interruptions (illness, parental leave, full-time care, military/civil service) by contacting the Fellowship Office BEFORE initiating the LOI and must enter interruption dates in the CV section. Interruption periods NOT eligible: unemployment, volunteer work, internships, or any form of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-author original research publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have at least ONE full-length original research publication in English for which the applicant is a lead author (single, first, or joint-first author). Review articles and patents do not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the LOI stage acceptable evidence is: (i) published in a peer-reviewed journal; (ii) accepted/in press; (iii) accepted for publication; or (iv) available online in a recognized OA preprint repository AND submitted to a peer-reviewed journal. Manuscripts that have not been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, or are in review but not available as an OA preprint, do NOT qualify at any stage. At the Full Proposal stage, OA preprints alone are NOT valid—applicants must have a lead-author manuscript published, accepted, or in press. If field conventions (e.g., alphabetical authorship) make first authorship impossible, explain in the “Additional Comments” field; also explain articles that lack DOIs if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope: basic life-sciences research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports basic research studying fundamental problems in the life sciences at all levels (genes, molecules, biophysics, intracellular networks, tissues/organs, organismal functions including cognition, populations, ecosystems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed research topic must be within life sciences and be basic/fundamental rather than purely applied. Applicants unsure about fit may contact the Fellowship Office for general feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not supported: excluded research topics and approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP does not fund projects of a purely applied nature or certain specified topics and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of not funded research: projects with a primarily clinical and/or pharmaceutical focus (diagnosis, treatment, drug targets, drug design/development); applied projects in engineering, biotechnology, or nanotechnology; development of novel methods that do not aim to answer a basic biological question; projects directly focused on solving agricultural, forestry, environmental, or conservational problems; purely observational or descriptive projects including systematic screening and data-collection studies (genomes, transcriptomes, connectomes, populations, ecosystems). Also not funded: projects that are an obvious next step in the host laboratory or a close continuation of the applicant's PhD or prior postdoctoral work; research in for-profit environments (though collaborations with industry are allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility screening and compliance checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All Letters of Intent and invited Full Proposals are checked for compliance with formal eligibility criteria; formally ineligible LOIs will not be further considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOIs are screened for alignment with HFSP objectives and scientific scope by a small review committee; applicants whose LOIs do not align will be notified. Eligible LOIs then undergo full peer review. Full Proposals are again checked for eligibility (notably publication requirements) before sending to external reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI review scoring and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each eligible LOI in scope will be assessed by two Fellowship Review Committee members who use an alphabetical score from A (highest) to D (lowest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the two reviewers' scores differ significantly, a third reviewer assesses the application. Reviewer scores are used to rank LOIs; typically the top 15–20% of eligible LOIs are invited to submit Full Proposals. LOI applicants will be notified between mid‑August and end of August whether their LOI was selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal external review and committee evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible Full Proposals are sent to external scientific reviewers (expected 2–3 evaluations). Two Review Committee members then evaluate each Full Proposal taking external reviews into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship Review Committee meets (early February) to discuss proposals; original committee members defend or revise initial ratings. Numerical scores from original committee members suggest an overall score; all members provide scores after discussion and average scores are used to generate a ranked list of proposals recommended for funding. Applicants are notified of outcomes once internal HFSP formalities are complete (usually towards the end of March).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship award conditions: duration and activation
rubrics_metrics.description: The HFSP Fellowship is awarded for 3 years (36 months) and cannot be renewed. Fellows must begin their fellowship between specified activation dates (e.g., between 1 April 2027 and 1 January 2028 for the 2027 cycle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PhD must have been conferred by the date of Fellowship activation. Appointment must be 100% FTE and allowances are administered through the host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances and administrative responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows receive a Living Allowance and a Research & Travel Allowance; depending on situation may qualify for Child Allowance, Parental Leave Allowance, and Relocation allowance. Allowances differ by Host Country and are administered through the host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows should investigate tax liabilities and visa costs. Full details and amounts are in the Application Guidelines and the Agreement/Conditions of Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferrals and interruptions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may interrupt ('defer') HFSPO support for up to two years (24 months) under specific circumstances after completing at least one year of the HFSP Fellowship in the proposed host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests for deferral require prior approval by HFSPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent employment and additional funding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Fellows cannot concurrently hold an HFSP Fellowship and another paid employment position or another paid fellowship from another organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HFSP living allowance can be supplemented from other sources (host supervisor’s grant or institutional funds) to meet host institution salary requirements, but additional research grants may not be used as the fellow’s salary. Fellows must devote themselves entirely to their research project and may not engage in other paid activity without prior agreement by HFSPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-year mobility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In the third year, fellows may continue in the same host lab, return to their or their partner’s home country, or move to another HFSPO member country, but moves require prior approval from HFSPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants do NOT need to describe or discuss proposed third-year activities in their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at HFSP Awardees Meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP regards attendance at its Awardees Meeting as important and HFSP Awardees will be invited to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are strongly encouraged to attend at least one HFSP Awardees Meeting during their award tenure; information regarding expenses is in the Agreement and Conditions of Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and explanation requirements for atypical cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must document and explain atypical circumstances affecting eligibility or publication records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if first-author publication is impossible due to field practices (alphabetical authorship), explain in the Additional Comments field; if publications lack DOIs or are in nonstandard formats, explain in Additional Comments. Applicants seeking exemptions for career interruptions must contact HFSP with dates and reasons BEFORE initiating the LOI and enter interruption dates in the CV section.
